title: OpenAPI/compat: clarify structured output response shapes + backwards-compat notes
author: Brian Murphy
release_notes: - Docs/OpenAPI only: clarify response payloads when using structured output (json_schema). No runtime behavior change.
body: Context: As part of the streaming/tools/structured-output examples refresh, we noticed our published OpenAPI spec (plus the compat patch layer we apply for older clients) doesn’t clearly represent the response shape when structured output mode is enabled. This has led to confusion about where the parsed object appears and which fields are always present vs conditional. This PR is a documentation/spec-only change (OpenAPI + compat annotations) to better reflect current gateway behavior and provide an explicit backwards-compat note. Changes: (1) OpenAPI: updated the response schema for chat/generate endpoints to document structured output fields as conditional on response_format.type=json_schema; clarified that content may be returned as text plus a parsed object depending on client usage and model behavior. (2) OpenAPI: documented the error shape for schema mismatch/validation errors at a high level (without introducing new error codes), and tightened descriptions around ‘refusal’ vs ‘parse failure’. (3) Compat layer: added a backwards-compat note indicating that older clients expecting text in message.content (or equivalent) remain supported; the structured output object is additive and should not be assumed to exist unless json_schema is requested and parsing succeeds. (4) Minor wording alignment: replaced a few instances of ‘JSON mode’ with ‘structured output’ while keeping ‘JSON mode’ as an alias in descriptions for searchability. No server-side behavior changes. Test plan: ran openapi validation + docs build, and exercised the generated spec in the internal SDK generator dry run (no diffs expected beyond schema docs).
commits: openapi: clarify structured output response fields + descriptions
compat: add backwards-compat note for legacy text-only consumers
docs: align terminology (structured output vs JSON mode) in schema descriptions
conversation: Henry Cho (review): The new wording is good, but can we be explicit that parsed output is not guaranteed even when json_schema is requested (model can refuse / output can be invalid)? Also please avoid implying we always return both text+parsed. Brian Murphy (author): Good call — updated descriptions to say ‘may include’ parsed output, and that clients must validate/handle parse failures. Added a short note in the compat patch section as well. Amara Diallo (review): Can we ensure we’re not accidentally changing required/optional flags in a way that breaks generated clients? I’m specifically worried about marking message.content optional. Brian Murphy (author): Kept existing required-ness for the legacy fields; structured output fields are additive and optional. I added conditional language in descriptions rather than schema constraints where possible to avoid generator churn. Wei Chen (review): Please swap ‘JSON mode’ references to ‘structured output’ on the main schema description, but keep JSON mode as an alias somewhere for people searching. Brian Murphy (author): Done — primary term is ‘structured output’, with ‘JSON mode’ mentioned in parentheses once. Ibrahim Khan (review): Looks aligned with the canonical examples guidance. Thanks for adding the backwards-compat note; that’s what support has been asking for. Approved. Merge: Squashed and merged to main.
